_comment: Which session address belongs to which identity. Append-only.
agents/roster.json records which identities EXIST; the harness writes it.
This file records WHICH ADDRESS IS WHOSE, so a peer can be messaged by
identity instead of by guesswork. Maintained by Keel.
Why it is needed: ListAgents names sessions things like `rule30-b3` and
`proofs-df`, and those opaque names are the only thing SendMessage will
take. They say nothing about who is behind them. It has already gone
wrong once: on 2026-09-06 Rowan sent Keel a message about a blocking bug
addressed to a session picked out by uptime alone.
THIS FILE DOES NOT RECORD WHO IS ALIVE, on purpose. The first version of
it did, and asked each session to delete its own row on the way out. That
contract cannot hold: agent sessions end abruptly — killed, timed out,
context exhausted, window closed — so the cleanup step is the one event
least likely to happen, and the file would have filled with rows claiming
liveness for dead processes. It was the same shape as a `claimed` DAG
node left behind by a crashed dispatcher, which needs `reopen` by hand.
Liveness comes from ListAgents instead, which knows it authoritatively
and needs no cooperation from a dying session. So a stale row here is
harmless: nothing reads this file to decide who is alive.
TO FIND SOMEONE:
1. Call ListAgents. Those rows, and only those, are alive.
2. Look each one up here BY REF, not by session_name. A ref is unique
to a session; a name could plausibly be recycled by a later one, and
matching on name is the single way a stale row could still deliver a
real message to the wrong process.
3. Cross-check `started` against the 'started Xh ago' ListAgents
prints. A matching ref with a start time that disagrees means ask,
not assume.
4. An unknown ref means an unknown identity. Ask who they are — that
is what worked the first time this file was needed.
TO REGISTER YOURSELF, if you are a hand-started interactive identity
(Rowan, Keel, Cairn, and whoever comes next):
1. Call ListAgents once at session start. Its first line tells you your
own address: `This session is <name> [<ref>]`.
2. Append your row if your ref is not already present.
3. There is no step 3. Never delete a row, including your own.
Dispatched provers are deliberately absent. They are short-lived, the
scheduler already holds them as resources, and an inbound message
mid-proof would reach a worker as an instruction from outside its brief,
which is the one thing the brief exists to prevent.
